en.text: The Joensuu Art Museum presents changing exhibitions in a former school building. The collection includes both Finnish works and ancient art treasures.

en.name: Näyttämö
en.text: Näyttämö is a cultural venue in Joensuu that focuses on performing arts. It regularly hosts theatrical performances and various creative projects.

en.name: Pohjois-Karjalan kansanteatteri Pokka
en.text: The Pokka Folk Theatre of North Karelia offers local theatrical productions in Joensuu. It is an important part of the regional cultural scene and promotes community theatre.

en.name: Vapaudenpuisto
en.text: Vapaudenpuisto (Freedom Park) is a central green space in Joensuu. It serves as a place of tranquility and houses several monuments in the heart of the city.

en.name: Pakkahuone
en.text: Pakkahuone in Joensuu is a cultural center located in a historic customs building. It is known for handicraft exhibitions and various cultural events.

en.name: Tiedepuisto
en.text: Tiedepuisto in Joensuu is an innovation center and science park. It houses numerous technology companies and promotes scientific collaboration.

en.name: Punaisten hautamuistomerkki
en.text: This monument in Joensuu commemorates the fallen members of the Red Guard. It is located at a historical burial site and serves for respectful remembrance.

en.name: Cosmic
en.text: Cosmic is a popular leisure center in Joensuu offering bowling and other activities. It is an ideal spot for entertainment and social gatherings in the city.

en.name: Taito galleria
en.text: Taito Galleria in Joensuu presents high-quality Finnish handicrafts. Visitors can see changing exhibitions and purchase local craft products here.

en.name: Kankaanrinnan huvila
en.text: The ruins of Kankaanrinta villa in Joensuu are the remains of a historic building. The site offers an interesting insight into the local architectural history of the region.

en.name: Puolesta Heimon ja Isänmaan 1939-1945
en.text: This monument in Joensuu is dedicated to the victims of the years 1939-1945. It honors the efforts for kin and fatherland and is a significant place of remembrance.

en.name: Joensuun Vapaaseurakunta
en.text: The Joensuu Free Church is a place of prayer and community in the city center. It offers regular religious services and various social activities.

en.name: Joensuun ev.-lut. kirkko
en.text: The Joensuu Evangelical Lutheran Church is a prominent brick building in the cityscape. It is the main place of worship for the parish and an important architectural landmark.

en.name: Pyhän Nikolaoksen kirkko
en.text: St. Nicholas Church in Joensuu is a beautiful example of Orthodox sacred architecture. It is known for its traditional construction and valuable icons.

en.name: Pielisensuun kirkko
en.text: Pielisensuu Church in Joensuu is a modern Lutheran place of worship with distinctive architecture. It serves as a religious center for the community in the Pielisensuu district.

en.name: Joensuun helluntaiseurakunta
en.text: The Joensuu Pentecostal Church provides space for worship and Christian community work. The building is an important meeting point for the local Pentecostal movement.

en.name: Market Square
en.text: The Market Square in Joensuu is the vibrant heart of the city, where regional products are offered. Visitors can enjoy the local atmosphere and taste typical specialties here.

en.name: Karsikon uimaranta
en.text: A public swimming spot for residents and visitors in the Karsikko district of Joensuu.

descriptionAdvanced.de: Joensuu ist die Hauptstadt der Region Nordkarelien und liegt an der Mündung des Flusses Pielisjoki in den See Pyhäselkä. Die Stadt wurde 1848 von Zar Nikolaus I. von Russland gegründet und entwickelte sich dank ihrer strategischen Lage schnell zu einem bedeutenden Zentrum für den Holzhandel. Im späten 19. Jahrhundert war Joensuu einer der wichtigsten Exporthäfen für finnisches Holz, begünstigt durch den Bau des Saimaa-Kanals. Heute ist die Stadt vor allem als lebendiges Bildungszentrum bekannt, in dem ein großer Teil der Bevölkerung aus Studenten der Universität Ostfinnland besteht. Kulturell ist Joensuu eng mit der karelischen Identität verbunden, was sich in der lokalen Küche und dem Kunsthandwerk widerspiegelt. Ein jährliches Highlight ist das Ilosaarirock-Festival, eines der ältesten Rockfestivals Finnlands. Die Umgebung bietet weite Wildnisgebiete, die für die Forstwirtschaft und den Outdoor-Tourismus von zentraler Bedeutung sind.
descriptionAdvanced.hu: Joensuu Észak-Karélia tartomány székhelye, amely a Pielisjoki folyó torkolatánál, a Pyhäselkä-tó partján fekszik. A várost 1848-ban I. Miklós orosz cár alapította, és stratégiai elhelyezkedésének köszönhetően gyorsan a faipar és a kereskedelem központjává vált. A 19. század végén Joensuu Finnország egyik legfontosabb exportkikötője volt, amit a Saimaa-csatorna megnyitása tovább ösztönzött. Napjainkban a város vibráló egyetemi központként ismert, ahol a lakosság jelentős részét a Kelet-finnországi Egyetem hallgatói teszik ki. Kulturális szempontból Joensuu szorosan kötődik a karéliai hagyományokhoz, ami az építészetben és a helyi gasztronómiában is megmutatkozik. Itt rendezik meg minden évben az Ilosaarirock fesztivált, amely az ország egyik legrégebbi és legnépszerűbb könnyűzenei eseménye. A várost övező hatalmas erdőségek a finn erdőgazdálkodás és a természetközeli turizmus alapját képezik.
descriptionAdvanced.ro: Joensuu este capitala regiunii Carelia de Nord, situat la gura de vărsare a râului Pielisjoki în lacul Pyhäselkä. Orașul a fost fondat în 1848 de țarul Nicolae I al Rusiei, dezvoltându-se rapid ca un centru vital pentru industria lemnului datorită accesului la căile navigabile. La sfârșitul secolului al XIX-lea, Joensuu a devenit unul dintre cele mai importante porturi de export din Finlanda, beneficiind de conexiunea prin Canalul Saimaa. În prezent, orașul este cunoscut ca un hub educațional dinamic, având o populație tânără datorită prezenței Universității Finlandei de Est. Identitatea culturală locală este profund marcată de tradițiile careliene, vizibile în gastronomie și festivalurile folclorice. Anual, orașul găzduiește Ilosaarirock, unul dintre cele mai vechi festivaluri de muzică rock din țară. Geografia zonei este definită de păduri vaste și râuri repezi, fiind un punct strategic pentru cercetarea forestieră la nivel european.
descriptionAdvanced.en: Joensuu is the capital of the North Karelia region, located at the mouth of the Pielisjoki River on the shores of Lake Pyhäselkä. The city was established in 1848 by Tsar Nicholas I of Russia and quickly emerged as a major hub for the timber trade and river transport. During the late 19th century, Joensuu became one of Finland's busiest ports, significantly boosted by its connection to the Saimaa Canal system. Today, it is recognized as a vibrant university city, with students from the University of Eastern Finland making up a large portion of its population. The city's culture is deeply rooted in Karelian heritage, often reflected in its distinctive local cuisine and artisanal crafts. Joensuu is also famous for hosting Ilosaarirock, one of Finland's oldest continuously running rock festivals. Surrounded by vast wilderness, the city plays a key role in European forestry research and outdoor tourism.
descriptionAdvanced.es: Joensuu es la capital de la región de Carelia del Norte y se encuentra en la desembocadura del río Pielisjoki en el lago Pyhäselkä. La ciudad fue fundada en 1848 por el zar Nicolás I de Rusia y se convirtió rápidamente en un importante centro para el comercio de madera gracias a su ubicación estratégica. A finales del siglo XIX, Joensuu era uno de los puertos de exportación más importantes para la madera finlandesa, favorecido por la construcción del canal de Saimaa. Hoy en día, la ciudad es conocida principalmente como un vibrante centro educativo, donde gran parte de la población son estudiantes de la Universidad de Finlandia Oriental. Culturalmente, Joensuu está estrechamente vinculada a la identidad carelia, lo que se refleja en la cocina local y la artesanía. Un punto destacado anual es el festival Ilosaarirock, uno de los festivales de rock más antiguos de Finlandia. El entorno ofrece vastas áreas silvestres que son fundamentales para la silvicultura y el turismo al aire libre.
descriptionAdvanced.pt: Joensuu é a capital da região da Carélia do Norte e situa-se na foz do rio Pielisjoki no lago Pyhäselkä. A cidade foi fundada em 1848 pelo czar Nicolau I da Rússia e desenvolveu-se rapidamente num importante centro para o comércio de madeira, graças à sua localização estratégica. No final do século XIX, Joensuu era um dos portos de exportação mais importantes para a madeira finlandesa, favorecido pela construção do Canal de Saimaa. Hoje, a cidade é conhecida principalmente como um vibrante centro educativo, onde uma grande parte da população é composta por estudantes da Universidade do Leste da Finlândia. Culturalmente, Joensuu está intimamente ligada à identidade careliana, o que se reflete na cozinha local e no artesanato. Um destaque anual é o festival Ilosaarirock, um dos festivais de rock mais antigos da Finlândia. A área envolvente oferece vastas zonas selvagens que são fundamentais para a silvicultura e o turismo de ar livre.
descriptionAdvanced.fr: Joensuu est la capitale de la région de la Carélie du Nord et se trouve à l'embouchure de la rivière Pielisjoki dans le lac Pyhäselkä. La ville a été fondée en 1848 par le tsar Nicolas Ier de Russie et est devenue rapidement un centre important pour le commerce du bois grâce à sa position stratégique. À la fin du XIXe siècle, Joensuu était l'un des ports d'exportation les plus importants pour le bois finlandais, favorisé par la construction du canal du Saimaa. Aujourd'hui, la ville est surtout connue comme un centre éducatif dynamique, où une grande partie de la population est composée d'étudiants de l'Université de Finlande orientale. Culturellement, Joensuu est étroitement liée à l'identité carélienne, ce qui se reflète dans la cuisine locale et l'artisanat. Un temps fort annuel est le festival Ilosaarirock, l'un des plus anciens festivals de rock de Finlande. Les environs offrent de vastes zones sauvages qui sont d'une importance capitale pour la sylviculture et le tourisme de plein air.
